test_text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. This is a test of text-to-speech synthesis quality and latency.

LINEAR16_PCM.description: Raw uncompressed PCM audio, 16-bit signed integers, little-endian
LINEAR16_PCM.streaming_suitability: EXCELLENT — lowest latency, no encode/decode overhead
LINEAR16_PCM.ws_considerations: Largest bandwidth; client must reassemble. Best for LAN/local.

WAV.description: RIFF WAV container wrapping LINEAR16 PCM with a 44-byte header
WAV.streaming_suitability: GOOD — simple header, then raw PCM follows
WAV.ws_considerations: Send header once, then stream PCM chunks. Easy client-side decoding.

MP3.description: Lossy compressed audio using MPEG Layer 3
MP3.streaming_suitability: MODERATE — smaller bandwidth but encode/decode latency
MP3.ws_considerations: Frames are self-contained; can stream frame-by-frame. Client needs MP3 decoder. ~26ms per frame at 128kbps.

OPUS.description: Modern lossy codec optimized for speech and low-latency streaming
OPUS.streaming_suitability: EXCELLENT — designed for real-time streaming, very low latency
OPUS.ws_considerations: Smallest bandwidth for speech. Native WebRTC codec. Ideal for WAN/mobile. OGG container not needed for raw streaming.

MULAW.description: G.711 μ-law companding, standard telephony codec
MULAW.streaming_suitability: GOOD — designed for telephony, very low latency
MULAW.ws_considerations: Fixed 8kHz/8-bit. Used by Twilio and PSTN gateways.
